report:
Conclusion: **Supported.** The adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV/Shingrix) substantially reduces shingles in adults ≥70.

The pivotal ZOE-70 analysis pooled 16,596 participants aged ≥70 from ZOE-50/ZOE-70 and found vaccine efficacy against herpes zoster of **91.3%** (95% CI 86.8–94.5; P<0.001), with efficacy against postherpetic neuralgia of **88.8%** (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800). The earlier ZOE-50 trial reported overall efficacy of **97.2%** (95% CI 93.7–99.0), remaining high across age strata (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25916341/). U.S. policy and labeling align with these data: CDC/ACIP recommends two RZV doses for immunocompetent adults ≥50, including those with prior shingles or prior live zoster vaccine (https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/67/wr/mm6703a5.htm), and FDA labeling states Shingrix is indicated to prevent herpes zoster in adults ≥50 (https://www.fda.gov/media/108597/download).

Caveats: trials mainly enrolled immunocompetent older adults; injection-site and systemic reactions are common but usually transient. RZV prevents shingles and complications; it is not a treatment for active zoster.
